finding.claim: --url silently sets allow_remote_refs=True, so a remote schema can make the generator read arbitrary local JSON/YAML mapping files via file:// $refs.
finding.source: Remote schema body served from the URL passed to --url; its $ref values are attacker-chosen (attacker controls the host, or MITM on plain HTTP).

trace.note: if config.url and config.allow_remote_refs is None: config.allow_remote_refs = True
base_url set: ref goes through join_url(effective_base, ref); absolute file:/// ref expected to pass through unchanged (not executed)
_get_ref_body: is_url() true, scheme 'file'; remote checks only apply to http(s)
block only when allow_remote_refs is False; here it is True so not blocked
_resolve_local_ref_path returns any path when allow_remote_refs is True; no base-path containment, no warning
_load_ref_data_from_path -> load_data_from_path (_source.py:246): file must parse as JSON/YAML mapping

finding.guards_checked: http.py:969-1027 SSRF guard covers only http(s) and never sees file:// refs. jsonschema.py:10932-10940 blocks only when user explicitly passes --no-allow-remote-refs (value False, not overridden). Parsed content must be a mapping, limiting readable targets.
